outcome: mode of birth (spontaneous vaginal delivery, cesarean section)
cohort: The study included 153 women who underwent labor analgesia at the University Teaching Hospital of Kigali.
finding: The implementation of a labor analgesia program was found to be feasible in a low-resource setting, demonstrating adequate pain control and a low incidence of maternal or neonatal adverse events.
mod_finding: Most women (67%) had spontaneous vaginal delivery, while 33% underwent cesarean section primarily due to non-reassuring fetal heart rate (58.9%) and labor arrest (19.6%).
